newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian insolvencies up 9.6 pct in first 9 months.
newsitem.headline: Austrian insolvencies up 9.6 pct in first 9 months.

text.p: A wave of insolvencies flooding Austria's businesses showed no sign of ebbing on Thursday when credit watchdog KSV said the number of company failures jumped 9.6 percent in the first nine months of the year.
KSV said 1,656 companies filed for insolvency in the first three quarters after 1,511 in the same period a year ago. Total liabilities fell to 43.2 billion schillings from 51.5 billion.
KSV said the figures include tour operator Itas, which on Wednesday filed for insolvency with debts of 1.28 billion schillings, making it the biggest failure to hit Austria's travel industry.
The biggest insolvency of the year remains construction group Maculan with liabilities of 11.1 billion schillings. Maculan's insolvency was the largest to hit a listed company since World War Two.
The second-biggest insolvency this year was also in the construction sector, namely Hamberger with liabilities of 1.33 billion schillings.
But Austria's largest insolvency since World War Two was last year's collapse of cooperative retail chain Konsum with massive debts of 26 billion schillings.
In 1995, there were 4,879 insolvencies whipping up 62 billion schillings in liabilities.
